title: Overload protection: Grafana dashboard + alert rules for breakers, shed rate, and queue depth
author: Sergio Costa
description: This adds the initial Grafana dashboard JSON + Prometheus alert rules for the Hosted overload-protection rollout (circuit breakers + load shedding). The goal is to make it obvious when we are shedding intentionally vs failing, and to page only when overload protection isn’t behaving as expected (e.g., breaker flapping, queue depth runaway, routing/control-plane health risk). Dashboard highlights: panels for admission vs served vs shed request rate; shed reason breakdown (gateway vs routing vs runtime) and per-reason series; circuit breaker state (closed/open/half-open) and transitions per (model, region, tier); queue depth and queue wait time (runtime + routing queues where available); p95/p99 latency overlays alongside shed rate; errors by HTTP code + Redwood error code (429/503) where present; template variables: region, model, tier, route, component, environment. Alert rules (defaults tuned for canary; see TODOs inline): 1) Breaker flapping: high transition rate open<->half-open or open<->closed above threshold, with cooldown window; pages SRE after sustained flapping (warn before page). 2) Shed rate too high for too long: sustained shed_rate > X% with sufficient traffic floor; routes to #eng-sre and pages when global for region/model (not per-tenant). 3) Queue depth runaway: runtime queue depth and/or queue wait time above threshold; pages when approaching tail-latency collapse risk. 4) Missing signals: breaker telemetry absent for a region/model where feature flag indicates enabled (catches mis-wiring). Notes: - Label/cardinality: intentionally excludes tenant_id / org_id from dashboard queries and alert groupings; all alert rules group by (region, model, tier) only. - These alerts are intended to complement (not replace) existing 5xx and latency SLO alerting; overload-protected 429/503 should not page unless accompanied by flapping/runaway conditions. - Next step: after us-east canary, re-tune thresholds and add per-model-class defaults (small vs large context window) + add a "control plane saturation" panel once Ethan’s metrics land.
commits: dashboards: add overload_protection.json with templating and base panels
alerts: add breaker transition + shed rate + queue depth rules
alerts: add recording rules for shed_rate and breaker transition rate
docs: add short README for importing dashboard and enabling alert rules
chore: wire dashboard UID + folder and validate JSON in CI
conversation: Aisha Bello (review): The dashboard looks good, but we should avoid alert grouping by route to keep pager noise down. Can we keep group_by to region/model/tier only and rely on dashboard for route-level diagnosis?
Sergio Costa (author): Yep. Updated all three alert files to group_by: [region, model, tier] only, and moved route breakdown to dashboard-only panels.

Allison Grant (review): Please double-check label usage. In a couple queries I see error_code + reason + model + region + tier all together; that’s okay, but avoid adding request_path/route_id and anything tenant-specific. Also suggest adding a recording rule for shed_rate to simplify.

Sergio Costa (author): Removed request_path usage (it snuck in via a copied panel), added recording rules: redwood_overload:shed_rate5m and redwood_overload:breaker_transition_rate5m, and updated alerts/panels to use them.
Logan Wright (review): For flapping detection, can you add a minimum traffic floor? Otherwise very low QPS models will show noisy transition rate.
Sergio Costa (author): Added traffic floor using served_rps > 1 (5m avg) as a condition for paging severity; warn still fires without the floor so we can see it in canary.
Christine Wong (review): Queue depth alert threshold: can we align with runtime bounded-queue defaults? Also, queue wait time might be a better primary signal than raw depth.

Sergio Costa (author): Updated queue alerts to trigger on either (queue_wait_p99 > 2s) OR (queue_depth > configured_threshold) sustained for 10m. Added links in comments to the runtime defaults in ENG-4826.
Aisha Bello (approval): Approved with the grouping changes.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. Thanks for tightening cardinality and adding recording rules.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved. Traffic floor addition makes sense.
release_notes: Added Hosted overload protection dashboard (breakers + shedding + queues) with region/model/tier templates
Added alerting for breaker flapping, sustained high shed rate, and queue runaway conditions
Added recording rules to keep alert expressions simple and reduce query load
